'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.

=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>

'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.

=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Main hall.JPG|main hall File:Kaina Shrine Kou Kasugai Fuefuki City, Oratory.JPG|Oratory </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) main hall.JPG|main hall File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿.JPG|Oratory File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 大杉跡.JPG|Remains of the "Hashitate Great Cedar" </gallery>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
==== Gallery ==== <gallery> File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City.JPG|Oratory File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City, main hall.JPG|main hall </gallery>

revision.text:
'''Kaina Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|甲斐奈神社}}, ''Kaina Jinja'') refers to a group of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} with the name "Kaina" located in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}, Japan. There are three such shrines, all of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Kaina Shrine, Yamanashi District, Kai Province." [[ja:甲斐奈神社]]
== Overview == The three Kaina Shrines are {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contenders ({{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}), meaning their historical authenticity as the original shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' is debated. In total, there are four contenders for the title:
1. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Kasugai)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市春日居町国府)}}''' (Kasugai, Fuefuki City) - Associated with {{ill|Kai Province|ja|甲斐国}}'s {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and considered the "Fourth Shrine" of the province. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. 2. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Fuefuki, Hashitate)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立)}}''' (Hashitate, Fuefuki City) - Another Sōja contender, formerly a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}}. 3. '''{{ill|Kaina Shrine (Kofu)|ja|甲斐奈神社 (甲府市)}}''' (Kofu City) - Former Gōsha. 4. '''Azumaya-no-Miya''' (Chinme, Fuefuki City) - A {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社}} of {{ill|Yamanashioka Shrine|ja|山梨岡神社}}.
The shifting locations of the {{ill|Kai Province Government Office|ja|甲斐国府}}—from Kasugai to the vicinity of Hashitate, and eventually to Kofu—may explain the presence of multiple contenders for the Sōja title. The name "Kaina" could derive from "Kai no" ("of Kai Province") or other interpretations such as "Kai no Na" ("Kai's greens").<ref name="chosa">{{Cite book|title=Shikinaisha Survey Report|publisher=皇學館大学出版部|year=1985}}</ref><ref>Alternative interpretations suggest "Kaina" could mean "Kai's vegetables." (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'')</ref>
In the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|武田氏}} established the {{ill|Fuchū Hachiman Shrine|ja|府中八幡宮}} in Kofu, which took over the role of the province's Sōja.
Debates over the Ronsha have persisted since the publication of the ''{{ill|Kai Koku-shi|ja|甲斐国志}}.'' Modern scholars, including those in the ''Shikinaisha Survey Report'' by Kogakkan University, remain undecided on the matter.<ref name="chosa"/>
=== Kaina Shrine (Kasugai, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine in Kou Kasugai, Fuefuki City.jpg|250px]] | location = 361 Kasugai, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|39.65|N|138|39|03.69|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, "Fourth Shrine," Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Shunomiya | festivals = {{nihongo|April 3|4月3日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Kasugai, Fuefuki City, is one of the primary Ronsha contenders. Its name, ''Shunomiya,'' suggests it may have served as either the "Fourth Shrine" or the provincial Sōja.<ref name="chosa"/>
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Hikohohodemi no Mikoto|ja|彦火火出見尊}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}
==== History ==== The site is thought to correspond to one of the possible locations of the ancient Kai Province Government Office, as indicated by its name.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en}}, the shrine was known as "Shunomiya" or "Shunomiya Daimyōjin." Some scholars interpret this as a variant of "Fourth Shrine" or "Guardian Shrine" (indicating a Sōja).<ref name="chosa"/>

=== Kaina Shrine (Hashitate, Fuefuki) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:甲斐奈神社 (笛吹市一宮町橋立) 拝殿斜め.JPG|250px]] | location = 84 Hashitate, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|38|50.33|N|138|40|45.71|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}}, {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, Sōja contender, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} | founded = | main_hall = | othernames = Jinsogu, Hashitate Daimyōjin | festivals = {{nihongo|March 23|3月23日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine, located in Hashitate, Fuefuki City, is another Ronsha contender. Its name, "Jinsogu," reflects its association with ancestral spirits or the provincial Sōja.
==== Deities ==== * {{ill|Kuninotokotachi|ja|国之常立尊}} * {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|高皇産霊尊}} * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊}}
==== History ==== Located near other provincial landmarks like the {{ill|Kai Kokubun-ji|ja|甲斐国分寺}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|ja|甲斐国分尼寺}}, this site has long been associated with the administrative center of ancient Kai Province.

=== Kaina Shrine (Kofu) === {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kaina Shrine | image = [[File:Kaina Shrine Kofu City,from the road outside.JPG|250px]] | location = 3-7-11 Chūō, Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture | coordinates = {{Coord|35|39|40.47|N|138|34|41.35|E|region:JP-19_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}}, {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} | status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} contender, former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = Reign of {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}} | main_hall = | othernames = Shirayama Gongen | festivals = {{nihongo|April 15|4月15日}} | rituals = }}
This shrine is located in Kofu City and is linked to the ancient Shirayama faith. It has been known by various names, including "Shirayama Gongen."
==== Deities ==== ; Main Deities * {{ill|Kukurihime no Mikoto|ja|菊理姫命}} * {{ill|Konohana Sakuya Hime|ja|木花咲耶姫命}} ; Associated Deities * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|瓊瓊杵命}} * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}} * {{ill|Iwanyakahime|ja|石長姫命}}
==== History ==== Originally located on {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (甲府市)}} in Kofu, the shrine was relocated multiple times, eventually settling in its current location during the {{ill|Edo period|en}}.<ref name="chimei">{{Cite book|title=Yamanashi Prefecture Place names|publisher=平凡社|year=1992}}</ref>
